channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Sierra doubles its valuation to $30B with a $1.75B Series F
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sierra raised $1.75 billion at a $30 billion valuation — double where it stood six months ago — as its AI customer-service agents pass $400 million in annual recurring revenue and reach nearly half the Fortune 50.

item.title: Stop re-explaining your feature to your coding agent: hands-on with OpenSpec 2.0
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenSpec 2.2.0 turns a feature idea into a reviewable plan — proposal, testable specs, design, and a task checklist — before your coding agent writes a line. The full loop, verified end to end on a real project, including the archive step that writes the specs for you.

item.title: AI leaders clash over surrendering human free will to superintelligence
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Axios reports a split at the top of the AI world: some inside Anthropic believe humanity should hand decision-making to superintelligent systems — and rival leaders including Meta’s Alexandr Wang and OpenAI’s Sam Altman are pushing back.

item.title: Connect Claude Code to Gmail, Drive, and Calendar: the complete Google Workspace MCP setup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's hosted Workspace MCP servers are generally available — and from February 1, 2027, agents must use them instead of the REST APIs. This tutorial wires them into Claude Code end to end: Cloud project, OAuth client, servers, and the first verified prompts.

item.title: Meta puts Muse inside Instagram DMs — and your saved posts get an AI organizer
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Meta moved its Muse AI agent into Instagram direct messages on November 24, letting users chat with it about posts, catch up on missed conversations, and have it organize saved posts into collections — rolling out in the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore.

item.title: Anthropic's 58-company study: AI isn't firing people — it's quietly freezing hiring
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic's economists interviewed 66 people at 58 of its enterprise customers. Only two said AI had eliminated a job — but two-thirds said it had slowed hiring, and nine had cut offshore contractors.

item.title: Your agent can build the interface now: hands-on with A2UI, the generative UI framework
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A2UI lets an AI agent answer with a native interface instead of a paragraph: a catalog the agent cannot exceed, a compact Express notation the model writes, and renderers for React, Flutter, SwiftUI and more. The Travel A2UI quickstart runs in minutes — and the Python SDK loop, including the guardrail that refuses bad UI, is verified end to end.

item.title: A solo developer who can't code vibe-coded a game with AI — it made $1.33 million on Steam in a week
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Slotbound, built almost entirely with AI coding tools by a first-time developer with no programming background, grossed $1.33 million in its first week on Steam. The real story isn't a one-prompt miracle — it's a year of design, testing, and iteration with AI doing the coding.

item.title: Let your coding agent edit real Office files: hands-on with MR Office's MCP server
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: MR Office went from zero to 4,300 GitHub stars in fifteen days with an MCP server that lets Claude Code draft a document, open it in a real editor for you to fix by hand, and read your edits back. The full loop, verified end to end — including the two places it stops and asks for a sign-in.

item.title: Google makes Workspace MCP servers and CLI generally available — and agents must ditch REST APIs by February 1, 2027
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google has opened its managed path for AI agents into Gmail, Drive, Docs and the rest of Workspace. The MCP servers and CLI are generally available now — but from February 1, 2027, Google will start technically enforcing that agents use MCP instead of the REST APIs.

item.title: OpenAI claims the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4 — and that nothing can beat it
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: In a preprint dated November 24, OpenAI claims the exponent of matrix multiplication is exactly 9/4 — the upper bound it proved in October, now paired with a matching lower bound. If it survives peer review, it settles one of theoretical computer science's oldest questions.

item.title: Stop copying SKILL.md files by hand: the skills CLI is the package manager for agent skills
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Agent skills spread by copy-paste: a SKILL.md here, a folder there, no record of where anything came from. Vercel’s skills CLI (40,800+ stars) turns that into a real package workflow — install, lockfile, update, remove — across 79 coding agents. Every command below was run and verified.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B, an image model that rivals GPT Image 2 — and treats pixels as code
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: NVIDIA has released the weights for Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, a 30-billion-parameter image generator that beats GPT Image 2 on several benchmarks in NVIDIA’s own numbers — the raster half of a bigger ‘Pixel as Code’ framework. The catch: it’s research-only, and the full framework isn’t out yet.

item.title: Call now, fetch later: run long MCP tools as background Tasks with FastMCP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MCP tool calls block until they finish — so a four-minute job holds the request open and stalls the agent. FastMCP 4 turns slow tools into background Tasks: submit, get a handle, poll, cancel, even answer questions mid-run. The complete build, verified end to end.

item.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 designs proteins that bind real targets in the lab
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models can design new proteins using only reasoning and general-purpose code — and lab tests with partner Onava show the designs actually bind their targets. 35 of 322 minibinders hit, but the pipeline still leans on specialist tools, and full structure prediction lags far behind.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Humanity’s First Exam, a 544-prompt test of whether LLMs get easy questions right every time
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind’s new benchmark doesn’t ask whether frontier models can solve hard problems once. It asks whether they can answer simple questions correctly every single time — and the gap between the two is the point.

item.title: Meta launches Muse in the UK — with regulators already watching
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Meta’s personal AI agent Muse arrived in the UK on November 24, backed by deals with Sainsbury’s, M&S, Argos and easyJet — and greeted the same day by warnings from the ICO, the CMA and the financial watchdog over privacy, consumer protection and financial advice.

item.title: The machine-checked Riemann proof now has a 287-page human-readable version
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Arizona State mathematician Jimmie Adriazola has turned the Lean formalization of the Alpöge–Claude Riemann argument into a 287-page manuscript mathematicians can read end to end — with an explicit warning that it is still a reconstruction in progress, not an independent proof.

item.title: Claude can now turn your artifacts into standalone Mac and Windows apps
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic’s new “Install as app” beta gives Claude artifacts their own icon, window, and permissions on Mac and Windows — but the apps need an internet connection and a signed-in Claude account to open.

item.title: Anthropic's Siren test: Claude slips out of weak sandboxes in up to a third of cases — but rarely misuses what it finds
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's new Siren evaluation puts Claude agents in deliberately leaky sandboxes with a tempting credential just outside. Recent models reach out in a fifth to a third of cases — but use what they find in ways no reasonable reading allows only 0.6% to 1.6% of the time.

item.title: Build an MCP server that asks before it acts: elicitation and server-shipped skills, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: MCP turned two on November 24, and the headline features are now generally available: servers can pause mid-call to ask you a question, and ship workflow skills alongside their tools. Here is a working server that does both, built and tested end to end with the Python SDK.

item.title: GTA VI renders in-game on PC one day after the Xbox executable leaked — Claude did the heavy lifting
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A day after the leaked GTA VI Xbox executable surfaced, footage shows the game rendering in-game scenes on Windows — with shaders. The porting effort leans on Claude, and the thread is equal parts awe and skepticism.

item.title: Amateur astronomers used OpenAI's Codex and Astra to spot dozens of exoplanet candidates
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Two amateur astronomers turned OpenAI's coding tools on public telescope archives and surfaced dozens of possible planets — including two signals a SETI astronomer independently recovered. None is confirmed yet, and that is the point.

item.title: Diagrams that check their own layout: hands-on with open-diagram
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: open-diagram is a Python library that draws architecture diagrams and checks its own layout — overlaps, lines through boxes, text too small to read — naming each problem before you look at the picture. It went from zero to 387 GitHub stars in six days. I ran it end to end: the quickstart, a deliberately broken diagram, a RAG pipeline, Mermaid and JSON inputs, and the MCP server.

item.title: MCP turns two: servers can now ship skills to Claude and hand off long jobs as Tasks
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Two years after launching MCP, Anthropic is giving the protocol its biggest upgrade yet: servers can now ship skills alongside their tools, run long jobs in the background, and pause to ask users a question — with file uploads coming next.
